instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 1.2 mL final-volume basis, charge benzyl azide: 0.3 mmol (0.25 M final); phenylacetylene: 0.33 mmol (0.275 M final); add acetone to 1.2 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation. The 1.2 mL basis is only the minimum consumed at the final feed rate during 2.4 min of commissioning and initial collection. Before preparation, add measured feed-line displacement, pump/reservoir hold-up and any extra startup or collection allowance. For an added duration, add this stream's flow rate multiplied by the extra minutes. Scale every solute amount and final solvent volume by the same factor to retain concentrations and reagent ratios. Confirm sufficient reagent availability and container capacity; no dead-volume allowance or available stock has been assumed. Provide priming and shutdown solvent separately. This schedule assumes continuous feeding; a finite sample-loop injection requires a separately specified loading and collection schedule.

parameter_bindings.minimum_stock_basis: continuous feed during commissioning plus initial collection

instruction: Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 20 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Minimize azide feed inventory and reactive holdup.
Stop feeds and cool before responding to blockage; never open under pressure.
Prevent unassessed metal-azide accumulation and stagnant zones.
Operate behind declared shielding or enclosed containment.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 1.8 min, using three times the larger of the declared total reactor-time index and the sum of stage volume divided by local liquid flow. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present. Budget additional feed for any extension before starting the run.

parameter_bindings.residence_time_basis: nominal empty-bed liquid space time (geometric reactor volume / liquid flow)

instruction: After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 0.6 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method, with feed stocks scaled to the revised duration.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.
Depressurize only through the controlled outlet while monitoring the pressure indicator; verify zero pressure before opening any fitting.

On leak, blockage, pressure excursion, or temperature excursion: stop reactive feeds and energy input, maintain only the hazard-appropriate purge/cooling path, isolate sources, and follow the laboratory emergency plan.
Collect product, flush, quench, and vent-associated waste in separately labeled containers compatible with the declared hazards; do not combine incompatible waste streams.
